doc_name: List of prime ministers of India
text: The prime minister of India is the chief executive of the Government of India and the chair of the Union Council of Ministers. Although the president is the constitutional, nominal, and ceremonial head of state, in practice, executive authority is vested in the prime minister and their Council of Ministers. The prime minister is elected by the party that secures a majority in the Lok Sabha, the lower house of India’s parliament, which is the primary legislative body. The prime minister and their cabinet are always responsible to the Lok Sabha. The prime minister may be a member of either the Lok Sabha or the Rajya Sabha, the upper house. The prime minister ranks third in the order of precedence. The prime minister is appointed by the president, but must maintain the confidence of a majority of Lok Sabha members, who are directly elected every five years, unless the prime minister resigns. The prime minister presides over the Council of Ministers and unilaterally controls the selection and dismissal of its members, as well as the allocation of government posts. The council is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3) and provides aid and advice to the president, which is binding under Article 74. Since 1947, India has had 14 prime ministers. Jawaharlal Nehru was the first prime minister, serving from 15 August 1947 until his death in May 1964, initially as prime minister of the Dominion of India and later of the Republic of India, following the 1952 general elections. He previously led the Interim Government of India from 2 September 1946 to 14 August 1947, after the Indian National Congress won the 1946 provincial elections. Nehru was succeeded by Lal Bahadur Shastri, whose one-year and seven-month term ended with his death in Tashkent, then in the USSR, where he had signed the Tashkent Declaration with Pakistan. Indira Gandhi, Nehru’s daughter, became India’s first female prime minister in 1966. Eleven years later, her party lost the 1977 general election to the Janata Party, whose leader Morarji Desai became the first non-Congress prime minister. After Desai resigned in 1979, Charan Singh briefly served as prime minister before the Congress won the 1980 election and Indira Gandhi returned. Her second term ended on 31 October 1984, when she was assassinated by her bodyguards. Her son, Rajiv Gandhi, became India’s youngest prime minister. Members of the Nehru–Gandhi family have served as prime minister for approximately 38 years. After Rajiv Gandhi’s five-year term ended due to a general election loss, V. P. Singh of the Janata Dal formed a year-long National Front coalition government in 1989. A seven-month interlude under Chandra Shekhar followed, after which the Congress party returned to power under P. V. Narasimha Rao in June 1991, following Rajiv Gandhi’s assassination. Rao’s five-year term was succeeded by four short-lived governments: Atal Bihari Vajpayee of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) served for 13 days in 1996, followed by one-year terms under United Front prime ministers H. D. Deve Gowda and Inder Kumar Gujral, and Vajpayee again for 13 months in 1998–1999. In 1999, Vajpayee’s National Democratic Alliance (NDA) won the general election, becoming the first non-Congress alliance to do so, and he served a full five-year term. The Congress and its United Progressive Alliance (UPA) won the 2004 and 2009 general elections, with Manmohan Singh serving as prime minister from 2004 to 2014. The BJP won the 2014 general election and formed the first non-Congress single-party majority government under its parliamentary leader, Narendra Modi. The BJP won the 2019 general election with a larger margin, securing a second term for Modi. After the 2024 general election, Modi became prime minister for the third consecutive time, leading a coalition government after the BJP lost its majority—only the second such instance in India’s history, following the first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.
